title: The Unquiet Portrait
premise: When a drowned man washes up in Hollowmere wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, coroner Tamsin Voss realizes the corpse is the spitting image of Elian Marsh—the witness who supposedly died three years ago, the night Tamsin helped fake his death to protect him from the town's founding families. As she investigates who knew about the switch and why someone is staging Elian's return, Tamsin uncovers that the 'accident' they covered up was murder, and that the real killer has been watching her ever since. At the annual Founders' Anniversary Dinner, where the town's secrets are toasted in public and buried in private, Tamsin confronts the killer—Elian himself, alive and unrepentant, who faked his own second death to frame the family that abused him. Tamsin must choose between exposing him and losing the only person who ever made her feel seen, ultimately arresting him while keeping enough of the truth hidden to protect the found family they built together.
about_author: Coral Coldharbour spent a decade as a rural records clerk before turning to fiction, a job that taught her how much of a small town's history lives in its filing cabinets. She writes mysteries from a converted chapel on the coast, where she claims the fog does half the plotting.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Tamsin Voss pulls a drowned man from the reservoir on an ordinary Tuesday, cataloguing his effects with practiced detachment—until she finds her own missing cardigan buttoned around his throat. His face belongs to Elian Marsh, dead three years by her own paperwork. POV: Tamsin. Beat: dread cracking through routine.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin walks the cemetery at dawn, confirming Elian's headstone still stands over a coffin she personally verified was empty. Flashbacks reveal she forged the death certificate herself. Her deputy, Ruth Okonkwo, notices her shaking hands but says nothing. POV: Tamsin. Beat: guilt resurfacing like something drowned.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Tamsin interviews the last people who saw Elian alive—including matriarch Verity Ashcombe, whose charity gala he'd threatened to disrupt before his 'death.' Verity's grief seems rehearsed; her grandson Dorian watches Tamsin too closely. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the sense of being watched begin.

chapters.title: Closet Full of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Someone has been inside Tamsin's house—not stealing, just rearranging: clothes shifted, photos turned face-down, a chair moved two inches. The intrusion feels intimate rather than threatening. Ruth insists on staying over. POV: Tamsin. Beat: safety of home dissolving.

chapters.title: Three Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter from Elian's perspective, three years earlier: terrified, bleeding, begging Tamsin to help him disappear after witnessing what the Ashcombes did to his sister. Tamsin's choice to falsify records is shown as mercy—and as complicity. POV: Elian (past). Beat: sympathy established for a liar.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Invitations arrive for the Founders' Anniversary Dinner, and Tamsin's name is printed where it never used to be—as family friend of the Ashcombes. Someone wants her at that table. Ruth digs into the reservoir's water levels and finds the body was placed there recently. POV: Tamsin. Beat: trap tightening politely.

chapters.title: What the Sister Knew
chapters.summary: Tamsin tracks down Mara Marsh, Elian's sister, living under a new name two towns over. Mara confirms Elian sent her money every month—until eight months ago, when the payments stopped. If Elian was alive then, who is in the ground now? POV: Tamsin. Beat: hope curdling into worse questions.

chapters.title: Dorian's Alibi
chapters.summary: Dorian Ashcombe offers Tamsin an alibi for the night of the drowning so unprompted it functions as a confession-shaped gift. He flirts, deflects, and lets slip that Verity keeps a locked study no servant enters. POV: alternating Tamsin/Dorian. Beat: charm as camouflage.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin Society
chapters.summary: Ruth discovers old town records: Elian isn't the first. Three deaths across fifty years share the same pattern—witnesses to Ashcombe scandals, all officially accidental, all with irregularities only a coroner would catch. POV: Ruth. Beat: the town's rot given historical shape.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: In her late mother's belongings, Tamsin finds unsent letters revealing her mother also knew an Ashcombe secret and chose silence—for survival, for Tamsin's sake. The theme lands: invisibility is inherited here. POV: Tamsin. Beat: personal history mirroring the case.

chapters.title: The Man in the Photograph
chapters.summary: A tourist's photo from the reservoir, posted online, shows a figure on the far shore the night of the drowning—wearing Elian's build, Elian's coat. He wasn't hiding. He wanted to be almost-seen. POV: Tamsin. Beat: realization that the dead man is directing events.

chapters.title: Verity's Study
chapters.summary: Tamsin breaks into the locked study during a power outage and finds files on every silenced witness—including a fresh folder labeled VOSS. Inside: photographs of Tamsin forging the certificate, taken three years ago. They always knew. POV: Tamsin. Beat: her protection was always their leash.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Mara calls: someone matching Elian visited her yesterday, left a note reading 'Tell Tamsin to bring the file.' Meanwhile Verity invites Tamsin to tea and thanks her, warmly, for 'everything you've done for this family.' POV: alternating. Beat: converging threads, rising panic.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: The Anniversary Dinner begins. Two hundred guests, crystal glasses, Verity presiding. When the toast is raised, the lights fail—and when they return, a portrait above the mantel has been replaced with a photograph of the drowned man, wearing Tamsin's cardigan. POV: Tamsin. Beat: public exposure as weapon.

chapters.title: Panic in Good Taste
chapters.summary: Chaos barely contained: guests whisper, Verity smiles harder, Dorian quietly locks the doors 'for security.' Tamsin realizes the dinner is a stage someone built for a confession—hers or Verity's. She slips away to search the cellar. POV: Tamsin. Beat: gilded pressure cooker.

chapters.title: Cellar of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: In the cellar Tamsin finds Elian alive, thinner, half-feral, holding the evidence file. He confesses: he killed the lookalike—a dying drifter paid by Verity to impersonate him—to force the town to reopen the past. POV: Elian. Beat: the ally revealed as murderer; heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Elian argues his case: the drifter was already dying, Verity's money bought his consent, and one death bought justice for his sister and three others. Tamsin hears her mother's letters in his logic. POV: Elian/Tamsin dialogue-driven. Beat: moral collapse of the reader's sympathies.

chapters.title: Verity Descends
chapters.summary: Verity interrupts, armed, having anticipated everything—she let Elian run because his confession would bury itself along with him. She orders Tamsin to choose: shoot Elian and join the family, or die as another tidy accident. POV: Tamsin. Beat: climax; the offer that names the book's price.

chapters.title: Glass and Gunpowder
chapters.summary: Tamsin shatters the wine cask instead, plunging the cellar into darkness and chaos. Ruth, who followed her, takes down Verity's armed caretaker. In the struggle Verity falls against her own display case—the Ashcombe legacy literally breaking around her. POV: Tamsin. Beat: action climax, loyalty proven.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Verity survives, charged; Dorian flees town; Elian turns himself in, insisting Tamsin take his full statement. She writes it honestly—including her own crimes—and hands it to the state investigator, choosing accountability over the comfortable lie. POV: Tamsin. Beat: costly integrity.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Months later: Elian receives a reduced sentence for manslaughter given Verity's documented crimes; Tamsin keeps her badge through a plea deal and community service. Mara visits Tamsin, and something like sisterhood begins. The town watches them both, but differently now. POV: Tamsin. Beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Unquiet Portrait
chapters.summary: Tamsin hangs a new photograph in her office—not of the dead, but of the living: Ruth, Mara, herself, taken at the reservoir shore in sunlight. She still knows every grave by name, but she's done filing herself among them. Final line echoes the opening: some portraits refuse to sit still. POV: Tamsin. Beat: found family, quiet peace earned.
